analysis.title: Charts: US Data Center Build-Out (Count, Capacity, State Mix, Value Erosion, Lead Times)
key_insights: US operating data center capacity is about 62GW versus about 386GW planned, roughly 6x the operating base (Cleanview, Apollo Chief Economist).
The chart pack counts existing data centers against announced/under-construction ones (axis runs to 4,500). The text gives no exact counts.
Texas has the most planned data center capacity by state (Cleanview), followed by Virginia, Utah, Ohio and Pennsylvania in the chart ordering.

Delays are the largest driver of AI data center value erosion. A 1.5 year delay cuts life cycle value by 8.9% and a 1 year delay by 5.5%, and a 6 month delay by 3.6% (Carnegie Endowment model, 100MW hyperscaler greenfield, GB200 NVL72).
Doubling electricity cost cuts life cycle value by 4.5%. Electricity +50% costs 2.2% and +25% costs 1.7%.
Removing state tax incentives costs 3.2% of life cycle value. Moderate server tariffs cost 1.7%, modest server tariffs 0.4%, and removing bonus depreciation 0.6%.
Doubling turbine cost costs 1.7% of value and doubling natural gas cost costs 0.2%. Climate-driven PUE loss costs 0.6%.

Supply chain bottlenecks are large: pad mounted transformers have the longest lead time in the chart set, at about 26 months on the high series and about 15.7 months on the low series. Generators and medium-voltage switchgear follow.
Lead times for electrical gear (medium and low voltage switchgear, UPS, switchboards) run well above those for materials such as copper wire and aluminium, which are under 2 months in the low series.
risk_factors: Construction delays are the largest modeled source of value loss for AI data centers, up to 8.9% for a 1.5 year delay.
Electricity cost increases are the second largest modeled driver, with a 100% rise costing 4.5% of life cycle value.
Long lead times for transformers, generators and switchgear constrain the build-out pace.
Server tariffs and the removal of state tax incentives or bonus depreciation reduce data center value.
charts_described: Chart 'US data center capacity growing from 62GW to 386GW' plots operating capacity at 62GW against planned capacity at 386GW.
Chart 'Impact of changes on U.S. AI data center life cycle value' ranks the modeled changes from a 1.5 year delay at -8.9% to natural gas cost +100% at -0.2%.
